TETANUS 
 
 
 
 
CAUSE 
*Clostridium tetani  
   à anaerobic spore forming gram positive bacillus 
*When spores germinate, and bacteria multiply à   
   toxins released i.e. tetanospasmin and tetanolysin 
 
TYPES 
*Cephalic / Local / Generalised / Neonatal 
CLINICAL FEATURES 
TRIAD – rigidity, muscle spasms & autonomic dysfunction 
 
* Contaminated wound may be trivial 
* Incubation period – 3-14 days à time to first symptom 
* Onset time – 1-7 days à time from first symptom to first spasm 
* Rigidity (persists > 2 weeks) 
 
-trismus, dysphagia, increased tone in trunk muscles 
* Spasms (reduce after 2 weeks) 
 
-laryngospasm, risus sardonicus, opisthotonos 
-may be spontaneous or provoked by physical/emotional    
   stimuli 
* Autonomic disturbances (onset after spasms – lasts 1-2 weeks) 
 
-tachycardia & hypertension may alternate with   
                 bradycardia & hypotension, dysrhythmia, cardiac arrest  
-salivation, bronchial secretions 
-gastric stasis, ileus, diarrhea 
* Respiratory compromise 
 
-chest wall rigidity 
 
-laryngospasm 
 
-aspiration 
 
 
COMPLICATIONS 
*Respiratory – aspiration, laryngospasm, apnoea, respiratory failure, ARDS, VAP 
*Cardiovascular – tachy/bradycardia, hyper/hypotension, ischaemia, cardiac failure  
*Renal – high output/oliguric renal failure, urinary stasis & infection 
*GIT – gastric stasis, ileus, diarrhoea, UGIB/LGIB 
*Musculoskeletal – rhabdomyolysis, fractures/tendon avulsions 2° spasms 
*Other – dehydration, thromboembolism, sepsis, MOD 
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS 
*Trismus 2° orofacial infection 
*Acute dystonic reactions 
*Hypocalcaemic tetany 
*Seizure disorder 
*Meningism 
*Psychogenic 
*Strychnine poisoning 
MANAGEMENT 
 
RESUSCITATION 
*Resus according to ABCs 
 
A – intubate as require high doses of sedatives to control  
                      muscle spasms and laryngospasm 
 
B – at risk of aspiration, copious bronchial secretions requiring  
                      frequent suctioning 
 
C – automonic dysfunction à monitor continuously,  
                      fluctuant haemodynamics so use short acting agents;  
                      fluid bolus PRN 
D – benzodiazepines in large doses (up to 100mg/hr Diazepam) 
 
SPECIFIC THERAPY 
*Metronidazole = 1st choice 
*Anti-tetanus immunoglobulin – 100-300IU/kg og human Ig IM 
*Benzodiazepines; alternative propofol 
*MgSO4 – useful in spasm treatment & limits autonomic instability 
 
TREAT UNDERLYING CAUSE & COMPLICATIONS 
*Clean & debride wounds (source control) 
*Immunize (infection does not confer immunity) – q10 yearly 
 
SUPPORTIVE CARE & MONITORING 
*FASTHUGS 
*calm environment 
 
DISPOSITION 
*Urgent ID/ICU referral 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
ED INVESTIGATIONS 
*U&E; CMP; CK; FBC 
*Blood cultures 
*ABG (respiratory failure) 
*U-dipstix 
*ECG
